messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Amy Liu <amy.liu@contoso.com>, Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@partnercenter.microsoft.com>
Date: 2025-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Azure Partner Center referral ops — Sprint 2 retro & tactical handoff

Hi team,

Quick retro from Sprint 2 and a concrete handoff plan for Contoso. TL;DR: mapping cleanup reduced owner ambiguity from ~18% -> 7% after the last reconciliation, but we still have 42 accounts in "unknown" state that must be routed to field sellers before next week.

Attachments: sprint2-retro-notes.xlsx (summary), pc-referral-mapping-v2.csv (current mapping snapshot).

Ask: Ben/Karthik — can you take the 42 unknowns and run the owner-fallback by EOD Monday? Prioritize accounts flagged as "containing prod workloads" in the mapping file. I've highlighted 12 P1 accounts in column H.

Amy/Matt — FYI, Contoso expects a one-week cadence for owner confirmation. If Partner Center needs additional consent steps, call that out in reply.

Proposed tactical handoff (short):
- Today: map-cleanup + confirm owner candidates (Ben)
- Mon morning: outbound asks to seller owners + cc AM (Karthik)
- Tue: final owner confirmation and transform to handoff-checklist.pdf for CS/AM

If we can't find owners for certain accounts, we fallback to the "cloud field default" routing (see retro notes). I'll run the canary for three P1 accounts to validate.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0117

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Amy Liu <amy.liu@contoso.com>
Date: 2025-06-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Partner Center referral ops — Sprint 2 retro & tactical handoff

Vanessa,

Got it — will start triage right away. Quick notes after skimming the mapping:
- The 42 unknowns appear to be concentrated in two Contoso business units (RetailOps / CloudInfra) — column F shows the team tag.
- 8 of those have recent PC referrals with seller-less status (no seller consent). I will ping Partner Center (Matt) for consent flow clarifications.

Plan: I'll split the list and do owner candidate discovery this afternoon/tomorrow morning. I'll use the PC owner history + LinkedIn + internal seller rosters. For the P1 canary, I suggest we route first to the assigned AM and CC the field seller candidate.

Attaching the mapping with my inline flags: pc-referral-mapping-v2.csv (see column J).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@partnercenter.microsoft.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Partner Center referral ops — Sprint 2 retro & tactical handoff

Ben/Vanessa,

Thanks — looping Matt for the consent clarification so Ben doesn't get blocked. Matt — short question: when Partner Center referrals arrive without seller consent, do we see a programmatic history (events) that would let us infer a likely seller (last editor, submitter) or do we need explicit consent each time? If there's a last-touch event we can automate tentative owner assignments.

Also, Ben — if you hit accounts that are multi-tenant (Contoso + Contoso Retail) mark them as split and create two inbound tickets — the mapping file schema has a "split_tag" flag you can use.

I'll take the outbound messaging template and run a canary draft for the 3 P1 accounts and share the draft in Drive. Will include the handoff-checklist.pdf as the final artifact.

Karthik Iyer
Partner GTM | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@partnercenter.microsoft.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Amy Liu <amy.liu@contoso.com>
Date: 2025-06-15T12:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure Partner Center referral ops — Sprint 2 retro & tactical handoff

Karthik/Ben,

Short answer: there are event-level breadcrumbs in Partner Center for referrals (submitter, last editor, consent timestamp) but consent is explicit for seller handoff. You can use the submitter/last editor heuristics as a "most-likely" owner and then run an explicit consent e-mail flow via the Partner Center owner consent API. I'll open a support ticket (928174) to increase the rate limit for owner-consent emails for your tenant for the next 48 hours.

For the automation path: export the referral events (we can provide CSV) and map submitter_id -> seller roster. If you want, I can arrange a short call to walk through the export fields.

—Matt Hayes
Partner Center Program Manager | Microsoft Partner Center
matt.hayes@partnercenter.microsoft.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Azure Partner Center referral ops — Sprint 2 retro & tactical handoff

Thanks everyone — quick status & next steps: 

Status snapshot:
- Ben: owner candidates identified for 37/42 unknowns; 5 remain (mainly split-tenancy, need AM confirmation).
- Karthik: drafted outbound messaging and canary template; shared canary in Drive (link in related_links).
- Matt: support ticket 928174 opened to lift consent email rate limits; partner center export fields confirmed.

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Ben: run owner-consent flow for 37 candidates using Partner Center API (start Tue morning). Track responses in column K of the mapping csv.
2) Karthik: finalize handoff-checklist.pdf and add the 3 P1 canary outcomes. Drop the final artifact in Drive and ping CS.
3) Vanessa/Laura: review any contested accounts (the 5 left) and escalate to Contoso AMs for split-tenancy confirmation.

I've attached the final checklist template (handoff-checklist.pdf) and the sprint retro. If we see >10% unmapped next week we'll pause auto-routing and open an escalation lane.

If no objections I'll mark this thread as "handoff in progress" and archive the sprint notes.

Thanks,
Vanessa
